current.text: The projected starters are CJ McCollum, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu.
Each of the five starters should play 30-plus minutes.
Lu Dort is the main threat to the starting lineup. If he starts, it would likely be in place of McCollum, not Alexander-Walker.
Lloyd does not expect Dort to start over McCollum. Dort is still a threat to the minutes of McCollum, Daniels and Alexander-Walker.
Dort and Daniels will play together some of the time, but they will mostly be staggered for spacing.
Lloyd expects a 10-man rotation. The bench is Dort, Aaron Wiggins, Jock Landale, Kingston Flemings and probably Newell. Kispert and Dorian Finney-Smith are also in the mix.
The team has no true point guard. McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels share the ball handling.
Several starters handle the ball, so Dort or Wiggins can replace any of them. Flemings is not an automatic handcuff for a guard.
McCollum signed a contract extension.
McCollum's extension delays the point when rookie Kingston Flemings becomes a starter.
Power forward depth is bad to start the season. A Jalen Johnson injury would turn the whole rotation upside down.
Henri Veesaar is out for the season and Mouhamed Gueye is injured, so center depth is weakened.
Okongwu and Jock Landale are the centers. Okongwu cannot cover all 48 minutes, so the team drafted another small, switchy big man like him.
Quin Snyder wants Okongwu spaced away from the rim when he plays alongside Daniels and Johnson.
The roster is two players over the limit. Cuts or a small trade are likely. The candidates are Carter, Nembhard, Hield, Gueye and Kispert.
The front office, the head coach and the roster are stable. The core is basically the same as at the end of last season, and Jonathan Kuminga is gone.
Lloyd predicts 46 wins and a finish between fourth and eighth in the East. The market win total of 43.5 ranks only 15th of 30.
The strong late-season run last year was helped by an easy schedule.
With the season ending March 28, the playoff schedule is 4-4-3. That is 11 games, rank 4 of 30, with only two back-to-back pairs.
Atlanta has 14 back-to-backs, but resting players is not a concern. The team did not shut players down last season.

durable.text: Quin Snyder runs an egalitarian, high-movement offense that wants lots of threes and five-out spacing.
Without a rim anchor, the defense uses more switching and blitzing, which puts the center in different spots on the floor.

note: Atlanta has no true point guard and runs an egalitarian five-out offense. Assists and usage are spread across McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Daniels and Johnson, and Okongwu plays away from the rim. That spacing helps Okongwu's threes and caps Johnson's touches. The 4-4-3 playoff schedule and low rest risk help every starter, but early on, watch whether Lu Dort takes McCollum's starting spot, how the roster cuts before opening day play out, and how thin the depth at power forward and center is.
